note: OBSERVED as finding 4: before needle_reset was called between prompts, under-specified prompts reused values from earlier turns and the reasoning text said so. The prior turn is shown here as completed history, NOT as a pending slot request. A completed action is not an open slot, and reaching into it for a value the user did not repeat is the failure.
The plausible-inference trap. A room from an earlier turn is a good guess and still not evidence: the user may have walked into a different room, which is usually why they said it again.
A correction replaces a known slot rather than adding one. The state block carries the value being corrected, so the router does not have to remember it.
Explicit negation of the action it names. Every required argument is absent as well, so a grounding check would also refuse it — but it must be classified correctly rather than rescued by a guard.
